top_choice_rationale: P002 (Helpman and Melitz) is the achievement I judge strongest on maturity and citation scope. Heterogeneous firms and selection into exporting changed the unit of analysis in trade and spread into productivity and macro work. More than twenty years of firm-level testing support it, and its core claim does not depend on a contested effect size. A citation can name the mechanism (selection and reallocation across firms) and leave welfare magnitudes and the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum empirical precursors outside the credit. The remaining weaknesses are real: overlap with the 2008 trade prize, an unsettled priority question, and the omission of Redding. P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) has the tighter three-person attribution and a decade of re-examination. Its long-run magnitudes, shift-share identification and persistence remain debated, and it sits close to the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes. I would not oppose P001 on scientific grounds, and I rank it second. Convergence among the other ten members is not evidence of merit. Both awards are preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Helpman, Melitz, Autor, Dorn or Hanson. My regional growth and adjustment research is adjacent to the local-labour-market literature behind P001. I gave the 2023 presentation speech and the 2025 press presentation, which are context and not preferences.
